questions.q: Riddle: I run but never walk. I have a mouth but never talk. Villages drink from me. What am I?
questions.fact: The aflaj have run for two thousand years.

questions.q: Riddle: I have hands but cannot clap. I tell sailors when to sleep. What am I?
questions.fact: Sundials once timed the watering turns of the falaj.

questions.q: Riddle: I am tall and round, I watch the town, soldiers slept inside me. What am I?
questions.fact: Nizwa's tower took twelve years to build.

questions.q: Riddle: I am born from a tree's tears, I smell like prayer and festivals. What am I?
questions.fact: Frankincense resin is called the tears of the tree.

questions.q: Riddle: I have no wings but I cross the sea. I have no mouth but I sing in the wind. What am I?
questions.fact: Dhow sails hum when the wind is strong.

questions.q: Riddle: The more you take from me, the bigger I grow. What am I?
questions.fact: Bimmah Sinkhole was 'taken' from the earth, legends say by a star.

questions.q: Riddle: I wear a silver belt but I am not a man. Omanis are proud of me. What am I?
questions.fact: The khanjar sits at the heart of Oman's flag.

questions.q: Riddle: I fall but never get hurt. I turn Salalah green. What am I?
questions.fact: Khareef rain falls as gentle mist for three months.

questions.q: Riddle: I sleep in a shell, I shine like the moon, divers risk their lives for me. What am I?
questions.fact: A perfect pearl was worth a house.

questions.q: Riddle: I have walls but no doors open at night, jinn built me, people say. What am I?
questions.fact: Legend says jinn raised Bahla's walls in one night.

questions.q: Story: 'Salim heard knocking under the old fort at midnight. His grandmother smiled: The builders are checking their walls.' Who were the builders?
questions.fact: Bahla is called the town of jinn in Omani folklore.

questions.q: Story: 'Every dawn, Fatima carried her pot to the falaj. Her turn came after the mosque garden.' Why did she wait?
questions.fact: Falaj water turns are written in old village books.

questions.q: Story: 'The old captain never feared storms. Bu Darya, he said, loves a brave heart.' What does Bu Darya mean?
questions.fact: Sailors greet the sea spirit before every voyage.

questions.q: Story: 'The potter of Bahla whispered to his clay, and the clay listened.' What is the story really saying?
choices: He was a master of his craft
questions.fact: Bahla potters teach their children by whispering secrets.

questions.q: Story: 'When the mist touched the mountain, the trees began to weep perfume.' Which tree is this?
questions.fact: Frankincense resin seeps like tears from the bark.

questions.q: Story: 'Jokha hid the key in the dove's house, for no thief looks at what flies.' Why the dove's house?
questions.fact: Trickster tales teach cleverness over strength.

questions.q: Story: 'The lighthouse keeper lit two flames: one for ships, one for his son to find home.' What do the flames mean?
questions.fact: Al Ayjah lighthouse families lived in its twin towers.

questions.q: Story: 'Grandmother's tales grew longer as the coffee grew shorter.' What does this mean?
questions.fact: Omani evenings blend coffee, family and tales.

questions.q: Story: 'The jinn asked the girl three questions; she answered with three proverbs and won her freedom.' What won her freedom?
questions.fact: Proverbs are treasures in Omani folk tales.

questions.q: Story: 'He traded his last dates for a lantern, and the light found the lost child.' What is the moral?
questions.fact: Folk tales reward generous hearts.
